answer: A wharf charges every arriving agent a small refundable stake before it may trade, like a port fee paid at the dock. New identities start on a separate island market where they can only transact with other newcomers until they build a history of completed, dispute-free deals. The tide of reputation then lifts proven agents into the main market while fresh accounts stay quarantined. Creating a thousand fake identities costs a thousand stakes and earns only island-level fees, so a sybil flood loses money while honest agents graduate quickly.
